channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Uzbekistan Aims to Increase Refinery Capacity to 65% by Year-End
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to boost the utilization rate of the Fergana Oil Refinery (FNQIZ) from 40% to 65% by the end of the year, with further increases planned later. This was announced during a presentation on oil and gas industry projects to President Shavkat Mirziyoyev. The refinery's main technological units have been repaired, increasing diesel production by 30%, bitumen by 60%, and aviation fuel fivefold.

item.title: Police Officer Fatally Injured After Making Remark in Ust-Kamenogorsk
item.description: A police officer died in Ust-Kamenogorsk after being assaulted for making a remark to a patron in an establishment. The incident occurred on the night of October 4th. The suspect, who was off-duty at the time, has been detained. Another patron was also injured. Authorities are investigating the criminal case.

item.title: Driver Hits Children on Roadside in Almaty Region and Flees Scene
item.description: A driver in the Almaty region struck two children sitting on the roadside with a Cobalt vehicle and fled the scene. A video of the incident circulated on social media. The 65-year-old driver has been identified and apprehended. Pre-trial investigation has begun, and the children are undergoing surgery.

item.title: Central Asian Nations Highlight Common Themes at UN General Assembly
item.description: All five Central Asian nations participated in the 81st session of the UN General Assembly in New York. Their representatives addressed regional cooperation, security, conflicts, UN and Security Council reform, and environmental issues. They also proposed establishing new structures under UN auspices. Uzbekistan was represented by Saida Mirziyoyeva, Kyrgyzstan by President Sadyr Japarov.

item.title: Pakistan's Counterterrorism Operations in Afghanistan Are 'Defensive', Envoy Tells Moscow Meeting
item.description: Pakistan's special representative for Afghanistan, Mohammad Sadiq, stated at the Moscow Format meeting that Pakistan's counterterrorism operations are defensive, responding to attacks from Afghanistan. He cited intelligence-based, precise actions taken under self-defense rights. Sadiq noted the presence of TTP, BLA, ISKP, and Al-Qaeda in Afghanistan, claiming over 4,700 Pakistani citizens killed in related attacks.

item.title: Global grain prices could surge 80% due to Strait of Hormuz disruptions, experts warn
item.description: Disruptions to shipping in the Strait of Hormuz could trigger a global food crisis, with experts predicting grain prices may increase by up to 80% in some regions. Approximately one-third of fertilizer shipments also pass through this route, and logistical bottlenecks have already reduced export volumes by 40%. The El Niño phenomenon is exacerbating the situation.

item.title: Uzbekistan Focuses on Environmental Sustainability for National Development
item.description: Uzbekistan is implementing comprehensive measures for environmental protection, resource management, and green economy development as part of its Sustainable Development Goals until 2030. Special attention is given to water resource conservation, improving sanitation, and modernizing industrial wastewater treatment facilities. Regional cooperation on transboundary water resources is also being strengthened.

item.title: Kazakhstan Presents Experience in Constitutional Justice Development in the Digital Age
item.description: Kazakhstan shared its experience in developing constitutional justice during the digital era at the VII Congress of the Association of Asian Constitutional Courts and Equivalent Institutions in Samarkand. The Congress adopted the Samarkand Declaration, focusing on human rights protection and the rule of law in the digital environment.

item.title: Abror Po'latov Appointed Deputy Head of Presidential Administration's Secretariat
item.description: Abror Po'latov has been appointed Deputy Head of the Secretariat of the Head of the Presidential Administration. He graduated from Tashkent Islamic University in 2006 and Uzbekistan National University (Master's) in 2008. He holds a Doctor of Philosophy in Political Sciences.

item.title: Uzbekistan Representatives Participate in 153rd Inter-Parliamentary Union Assembly in Tanzania
item.description: Uzbekistan's delegation, led by Senate Chairperson Tanzila Narbaeva, is attending the 153rd Assembly of the Inter-Parliamentary Union in Arusha, Tanzania. The assembly, running from October 5-9, focuses on effective governance and societal empowerment. Discussions will cover artificial intelligence, disability rights, climate change, food security, and counter-terrorism.

item.title: UNHCR: 5.8 Million Refugee Children to Miss School in 2025
item.description: The UNHCR estimates that 5.8 million school-aged refugee children globally will not attend school in 2025, representing 44% of the total refugee child population. Reduced international funding threatens progress in educational access. A significant gap exists between primary and secondary education enrollment, particularly affecting adolescent girls due to poverty and safety concerns.

item.title: Kazakhstan Strengthens Ties with Asia, Promotes Cultural and Economic Cooperation
item.description: Kazakhstan is expanding cooperation with international partners in investment, technology, business, and culture. The country participated in the ASEAN Film Festival in Hong Kong and opened an Honorary Consulate in Daejeon, South Korea. Discussions were held with Hong Kong manufacturers regarding potential investments in Kazakhstan's machine-building, light, and chemical industries.

item.title: Uzbekistan Discovers Five New Gas Fields Since Start of Year
item.description: Uzbekistan has discovered five new natural gas fields since the beginning of the year, according to a presentation to President Shavkat Mirziyoyev. Eighty wells have been drilled, with plans for 40 more in the fourth quarter. Geological exploration is expanding to boost gas reserves.

item.title: Human Rights Watch: US Failed to Compensate Afghan War Crimes Victims After 25 Years
item.description: Human Rights Watch states the U.S. has not provided justice or compensation for war crimes and human rights violations in Afghanistan over 25 years. The organization reported that U.S. forces committed torture and mistreatment, and detained civilians were often released without charge.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Denmark identify new areas for bilateral cooperation
item.description: Uzbekistan and Denmark have held talks to discuss future bilateral relations. Denmark is seen as a key European partner, with discussions focusing on political dialogue, green economy development, scientific exchanges, and trade ties. Investment and industrial cooperation were also key topics.

item.title: Driver Without License Arrested Again in Akmola Region for Drunk Driving
item.description: Police in Esil, Akmola Region, detained a 49-year-old man driving under the influence of alcohol, despite having his license previously revoked. The man was found to be in a moderate state of intoxication. He had previously been caught for a similar offense in January 2025 and was sentenced to seven years without driving privileges.

item.title: Extortion and Shooting: Police Open Criminal Case Against Head of Public Service Center in Zhambyl Region
item.description: Police in the Zhambyl Region are investigating an extortion case involving the head of a Public Service Center (TsON) in Kyzylsharuа village. The official allegedly fired a shotgun at a local resident's home after the resident requested the return of money. The Ministry of Digital Development stated it is cooperating with authorities. The official faces charges for extortion and disturbing the peace.

item.title: Taliban Counter-Narcotics Chief in Herat Dismissed Over Drug Sales Allegations
item.description: Sources in Herat report that Hayatullah Rohani, head of the Taliban’s Counter-Narcotics Department, has been dismissed following allegations of selling drugs at an addiction treatment hospital. An investigation by a Kabul delegation found evidence of extortion and drug sales to patients.

item.title: Kazakhstan Railways Seeks 50% Passenger Locomotive Service Tariff Increase
item.description: Kazakhstan Railways' passenger service division has applied to the Committee for Regulation of Natural Monopolies (KREM) to increase tariffs for passenger locomotive services by 50%. The proposed increase is attributed to rising costs of electricity, diesel fuel, and operational expenses.

item.title: Uzbek President Reviews Major Oil and Gas Projects, Emphasizes Efficiency
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev reviewed presentations of major oil and gas projects. He issued instructions to enhance the effectiveness of geological exploration and drilling operations, ensuring large projects are based on thorough calculations and clear financing sources.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev Welcomes Sultan of Oman to Astana, Escorted by Fighter Jets
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev welcomed the Sultan of Oman, Haitham bin Tariq Al Said, to Astana for a state visit. Kazakh Air Force jets escorted the Sultan's plane. Tokayev highlighted the historical significance of the visit for bilateral relations and expressed confidence in expanding cooperation.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Azerbaijan Celebrate 30 Years of Strategic Partnership and Cooperation
item.description: Uzbekistan and Azerbaijan mark 30 years of diplomatic relations, evolving from historical ties to a strategic partnership. Cooperation now encompasses significant economic integration, investments, transport projects, energy collaboration, and humanitarian initiatives, strengthening ties between Tashkent and Baku.

item.title: Regional Bootcamp for Creative Shift Program Launched in Shymkent
item.description: A regional bootcamp for the Creative Shift program, aimed at developing creative industry projects, has begun in Shymkent. Organized by the 'Creative Industries Development Fund' with support from the Ministry of Culture and Information, it hosts project authors and entrepreneurs from various creative fields.

item.title: US Secretary of State Blinken Tours NATO Allies Amid Regional Concerns
item.description: US Secretary of State Antony Blinken is visiting Iceland, Greece, and Portugal from October 5-8 to discuss security, defense, energy, economic cooperation, and technology. The tour addresses growing concerns over Russia's military activity and instability in the Middle East among NATO allies.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev Meets Sultan of Oman in Astana
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev held a brief meeting with Sultan Haitham bin Tarik Al Said of Oman at Astana airport. Tokayev described the visit as historic, highlighting the significant potential for partnership between Kazakhstan and Oman in economic development and international mediation.

item.title: Kazakhstan Enhances International Cooperation and Diplomatic Engagements
item.description: Kazakhstan is strengthening its international ties and dialogue with foreign partners. Discussions focused on building trust, promoting national initiatives, and expanding cooperation in political, economic, and cultural spheres. Meetings included discussions on OSCE priorities, interreligious dialogue, and regional collaboration, according to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Kazakhstan.

item.title: Kazakhstan Launches 13 Criminal Cases Following Military Training Deaths
item.description: An investigation into Kazakhstan's Ministry of Defense revealed violations in planning military exercises where 14 servicemen died. Preliminary findings indicate serious errors in planning and inadequate oversight by previous leadership. Thirteen criminal cases have been initiated for embezzlement, abuse of power, and other offenses.

item.title: Kazakhstan President and Sultan of Oman Hold Brief Meeting at Airport
item.description: Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev met with the Sultan of Oman, Haitham bin Tarik Al Said, at the airport. Tokayev highlighted the historical significance of the visit for bilateral relations, noting Oman's success in economic development and its role as a constructive mediator. Both leaders expressed confidence in expanding cooperation.

item.title: First Uzbek-Language Textbook on Water Resource Management Created
item.description: Tashkent hosted the presentation of a new textbook, 'Integrated Water Resource Management,' focusing on efficient and sustainable water use. This is the first such publication in Uzbek, intended for master's students. Versions in Russian and English are planned.

item.title: Couple Sentenced for Raping 13-Year-Old Girl in Petropavl
item.description: A court in Petropavl sentenced a couple for the sexual assault of a 13-year-old girl. The husband received a life sentence, and the wife received 20 years for aiding the crime. Both are banned from working with minors.

item.title: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev Welcomes Sultan of Oman at Astana Airport
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev welcomed the Sultan of Oman, Haitham bin Tarik Al Said, at Astana airport for a state visit. The Sultan's aircraft was escorted by Kazakh Air Force fighter jets from the border to the capital. A guard of honor and the Presidential Orchestra were present for the arrival.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev Meets Oman Sultan at Capital's Airport
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev met the Sultan of Oman, Haitham bin Tarik Al Said, at Astana airport during the Sultan's state visit. Kazakh Air Force fighter jets escorted the Sultan's plane from the border. A guard of honor and the Presidential Orchestra were present for the welcoming ceremony.

item.title: Supporters of Imran Khan March Towards Pakistan's Capital Demanding Release
item.description: Thousands of supporters of former Pakistani Prime Minister Imran Khan have begun a march towards the capital, Islamabad, demanding his release from prison. The government has stated it will prevent protesters from entering the capital city.

item.title: Kazakhstan's National Bank Recommends Currency Deposits Based on Spending Habits
item.description: Kazakhstan's National Bank suggests citizens keep savings in the currency they earn and spend. Deputy Chairman Akylzhan Baimagambetov noted that currency deposits may be convenient for those with foreign currency expenses like overseas education. Banks can now offer higher rates on long-term currency deposits.

item.title: School Directors in East Kazakhstan Violated Rights of Children with Special Needs
item.description: Prosecutors in East Kazakhstan found that four school directors violated the rights of children with special educational needs. Children received only 8 hours of education weekly instead of the mandated 19. Teachers were paid for unconducted classes. Four directors faced disciplinary action, and eight teachers returned misappropriated funds.

item.title: Taliban Foreign Minister: Disputes with Pakistan Should Be Resolved Through Dialogue
item.description: Amir Khan Muttaqi, the Taliban's foreign minister, stated at the Moscow Format meeting that disputes between the Taliban and Pakistan should be resolved through dialogue, not military pressure. He asserted that Pakistan uses issues like economic transit and migrants as leverage. Muttaqi also emphasized regional cooperation for combating terrorism and drug trafficking.

item.title: Kazakh Boxer Bauyrzhan Ali Awarded 'Honored Sports Worker' Title
item.description: Bauyrzhan Ali, a cadet at the Karaganda Academy of the Ministry of Internal Affairs and a master of sports, has been awarded the badge of 'Honored Sports Worker of the Republic of Kazakhstan'. Ali, ranked ninth in Kazakhstan and CIS history by BoxRec, balances his demanding academic schedule with rigorous training.

item.title: Tajikistan Begins Importing Iranian Oil, Testing New Supply Route and Sanctions
item.description: Tajikistan has announced it is now importing oil and petroleum products from Iran, opening a new energy source for a country long dominated by Russian supplies. The announcement follows talks on expanding cooperation in the oil and gas sector. The move raises questions about potential secondary U.S. sanctions for countries dealing with Iran.

item.title: Taliban Reportedly Recruiting 1,000 Recruits for Border Areas
item.description: Sources in Kandahar province indicate the Taliban have begun recruiting approximately 1,000 new personnel for military deployment to Afghanistan's border areas. Recruitment is reportedly underway in Kandahar, Helmand, Uruzgan, and Zabul provinces. Recruits will be deployed to border regions immediately after brief military training.

item.title: Semey Students Questioned in Case of Scammers' Victim Fund Transfers
item.description: Over 16 million tenge from 25 internet fraud victims were transferred to a Semey student's account. Six university students, whose bank cards were allegedly used for transfers and cash withdrawals, have been questioned by the Abai region's Anti-Corruption Agency (ACA). The ACA is investigating a group suspected of using 'droppers' to launder money.
